Put the preferred spelling first; add spoken variants after |, separated by commas.

This dictionary helps OpenWispr recognize and spell names, acronyms, and specialized terms during dictation and cleanup. It stays active with custom instructions. The spelling before | is the final form; spoken variants after it are pronunciation and recognition hints only. Example: OpenWhispr | open whisper, open wisper. Older one-term lines still work.

Android’s battery saver can shut down OpenWispr’s background service to save power, which makes the mic overlay disappear until you reopen the app.

%1$d%% (smallest) to %2$d%% (largest); %3$d%% is standard. Changes apply immediately.

Say the trigger phrase, then one of these — applies to whatever’s already in the field, or to text you dictate right after the command:

• “%1$s, summarize this in two sentences”
• “%1$s, enhance the flow”
• “%1$s, translate to Italian”
• “%1$s, make this more formal”
• “%1$s, turn this into a list”

You can chain commands: “%1$s, translate to Italian and turn it into a list” applies them in order.
